answer: The farrier lifts the hoof, trims it, and nails the shoe while the horse shifts its weight. Proof of farrier certification via farriers registration council is a record of that work: a certification the farriers council has renewed after every shoeing exam. One forged shoeing takes a hammer and a lie. A hundred take a hundred horses, a hundred hooves the farrier never touched, and the horizon of each is the nail hole in the wall — the quill is the owner who held the lead rope, the pearl the anvil, still warm from the forge.
